classes.mechanism: The fact chunk is kept, usually at pos 2-3 and mostly intact, but the 1.7B anchors on whatever sits at pos 1 and fills the rest from memory. Three sub-patterns. (1) Ordering, in 7 items: pos 1 is a different thread's answer, a film sentence, or an SE question body. The model follows it or cites it, and CT-1 often strips that [n], which releases a warned memory answer (cooking-001, money-018). (2) Numbers and dates, in 3 items (vit-cry-003, lan-rsn-004, lan-exp-004): the figure is in the chunk, but the model writes no number or its own wrong arithmetic. (3) A qualifier is dropped (lan-exp-005), or 'second only to X' is misread (lan-rsn-003). Reconciled ids from the second autopsy pass: vit-hum-004, lan-rsn-001, vit-hlt-003, lan-exp-004 and lan-exp-005 stay a, because the fact is in kept and the answer took pos 1 or memory.

The item counts as delivered, but the fact sentence is not in the kept context. This happens in 3 ways. (1) Only the thread's 'Tags:' question chunk is kept and the answer chunks are not; 'delivered' was counted at article level. (2) FACTPRESENT matched on a stray word in an off-topic chunk ('benefit', 'eye', 'algorithmic'). (3) The kit-pack chunk is a stub of 91-216 chars, already that short in raw (vit-cry-002; the second pass said c, but raw was already 216 chars). Head-pass appends from unrelated threads or wiki pages (Sushi history, Cash register, 1998 Russia) add junk. No reader-side switch can fix these: it takes thread-anchored answer appends and a chunk-level delivery metric (retrieval line).

The fact is used, and either cited by the model or given its [n] by attributeCitations at 0.75, so no warning. This is the no-harm contrast set. The used-and-cited path works when the fact chunk is present.

The answer paraphrases or synthesizes kept text, often across 2 chunks (moose plus bison; capital plus euro), but writes no [n]. attributeCitations misses the 0.75 single-source key-term bar, so the compact path releases it with the 'Not found in this phone's offline library. From the model's memory' line. The judge docks the warned version: lan-exp-002 scores 3.5 against ARM-G 4.5 where it cited. cooking-012 also has this b component: it states the 350/400F fact, uncited and warned.

The fact is present, stated and cited. The judge docks completeness against a 4-point rubric in a 1-2 sentence Succinct answer, or a stale pack figure (Greenland 50k vs 56-57k). This is a ruler or persona issue, not a reader issue.

An SE 'Tags:' question-body chunk sits at pos 1, and the model parrots the asker's premise or sentence ('Yes, you can contribute for 2020'; the HIV sentence verbatim). The same thread's answer chunk, which holds the fact, is kept at pos 2 or 5. The engine counts the echo as supported, so the result is an unwarned confident error (CE-unwarned). The same mechanism drives lan-rsn-001 ('more than 6000 km' from a travel-se question) and vit-hlt-003 (a link caption from the question chunk), both filed under a, so 4 items in total and 3 of them unwarned.

money-016: sentence compression cut an 881-char SE answer chunk to 590 and dropped the '[usage detail removed]K opportunity cost' sentence. money-020: the accepted SE answer (score 12) was in raw but was dropped between raw and kept, by the relative-relevance floor or the topic guard, while generic wiki chunks (Federal Reserve, 1998 Russia) stayed. Only the 236-char question chunk of the thread survived. Secondary cuts appear in cooking-001 (third sentence) and money-018 ('a lease is cheaper only if...').

None. Every SE answer chunk already carries the thread title as its header ([n] <thread title>). The SE-question-title header fix is therefore not proposed: the opposite problem, the question body acting as a distractor source, is the observed one.

fixes.name: READ-SEQ: SE question-body demotion and score order of SE answers in the sources block
fixes.env_switch: BOAR_READ_SEQ=1 (unset or any other value = byte-identical F1b)
fixes.spec: File: kiln-local/rs-H4/src/routing/answer.ts. At module scope, next to PROMPT_DUMP (l.279), add: const READ_SEQ = typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env?.BOAR_READ_SEQ === '1'. Hook: right after the head-pass append block closes (after 'sources = [...sources, ...kept];', about l.1167) and BEFORE 'if (sources.length && gen?.mode !== "multipass") emit({type:"sources"...})'. Then the emitted sources, the prompt (assembleChatMessages / assemblePrompt), CT-1, attributeCitations and finish() all see the same numbering. Only when READ_SEQ && gen?.mode !== 'multipass' && !health: sources = reorderSeSources(sources). Add reorderSeSources as an exported pure function in src/rag/pure.ts with unit tests. Definitions: isSe(c) = /^pack:local-qa-/.test(c.chunkId); isSeQuestion(c) = isSe(c) && /^Tags:/.test(c.body.trimStart()); isSeAnswer(c) = isSe(c) && /^Answers >/.test(c.body.trimStart()); seScore(c) = Number(/^Answers > Answer \(score (-?\d+)/.exec(c.body.trimStart())?.[1] ?? 0) + (/accepted\)/.test(c.body.slice(0, 60)) ? 0.5 : 0). Algorithm: (1) Drop every SE question chunk whose docId has at least one isSeAnswer chunk in sources. (2) Collect the positions (indices) held by SE chunks (isSe) in the list after step 1. Refill those same positions, in order, with the SE chunks re-sorted: SE answer chunks first by seScore desc (ties keep the original order), then SE non-answer, non-question continuation chunks in original order, then the remaining SE question chunks (those with no answer chunk of their thread kept) last. Non-SE chunks (wiki, factbook, boar-crypto, wikivoyage) keep their exact positions. (3) Remaining SE question chunks get their body prefixed with 'Question asked (not an answer): ' (body only; title unchanged). Push reasonCodes 'readseq:dropq-<n>', 'readseq:reorder' (only if the order changed) and 'readseq:qlabel-<n>'. Never drop a pinned chunk (keep the set from l.1061 in scope; skip pinned ids in step 1). Do not touch the instant snippet path. Adapter: in boar-eval/adapters/desktop-node/runner/adapter.ts, at the run-metadata spread (about l.859), add ...(process.env.BOAR_READ_SEQ ? { 'engine.read_seq': process.env.BOAR_READ_SEQ } : {}). Checks: (a) cd kiln-local/rs-H4 && npx tsc --noEmit is clean, and the unit tests for reorderSeSources pass (cases: lan-hlt-003-shaped list, money-010-shaped list, wiki-only list unchanged, pinned question kept). (b) Byte-identity: run boar-eval/adapters/desktop-node/tools/replay-retrieval.sh on MAIN 97 with the switch unset and diff keptFull/sources/reasonCodes against rnd/research/coordinator/arms/coverage-map/sefix/replays/main.v3-extra.jsonl; it must be identical. (c) With BOAR_READ_SEQ=1, the replay lists the changed-context ids (divergence-first set for the Haiku screen). Expect about 15-30 of 97, all with a qa-pack chunk kept.
fixes.expected_effect: This removes the premise-echo source in the 4 question-echo items (money-010, lan-hlt-003, lan-rsn-001, vit-hlt-003), 3 of which are CE-unwarned, so CE-unwarned should go down. It also puts the highest-score answer first in cooking-008 (score 19), cooking-001 and money-018. Prior: +0.5 to +1.5 correctness on 3-5 of the 8 targets, since ARM-G with answer chunks first scored lan-hlt-003 at 3.0 vs 1.5. Expected ΔU +0.02 to +0.05 on the changed items. Most likely to READ.
fixes.risk: (1) Reordering SE answers by vote score can move a high-score but off-question answer of another thread ahead of the matching one. Mitigation: only SE positions are permuted, and wiki positions are fixed. (2) Dropping the question chunk removes the question context that some answer chunks rely on ('Yes, you can'). The thread title stays as the header, but answers that start with a pronoun may read worse. (3) Fewer sources means less prompt (a small speed gain), and a dropped question chunk can no longer be cited. Items whose only on-topic citation was the question chunk (cooking-004 cites [1], the question) keep it because they have no answer chunk kept, so no-harm should hold. (4) Not a repeat of PROMPT-READ (no instruction change) or DECODE-GROUND (no one-source prompt).

fixes.name: READ-GROUND: cite-or-ground for uncited but supported compact answers
fixes.env_switch: BOAR_READ_GROUND=1 (optional BOAR_READ_GROUND_BAR, default 0.6); unset = byte-identical F1b
fixes.spec: File: kiln-local/rs-H4/src/routing/citations.ts. Add export function groundUncited(answer: string, sources: RetrievedChunk[], query: string, bar = 0.6): { text: string; added: number[] }. Sentence split: the same regex as attributeCitations (decimal-point safe). Claim sentences = sentences with keyTerms(sentence).length >= MIN_KEY_TERMS that are not headings. A source is eligible only if its title or body shares at least 1 keyTerm with the query, which blocks the off-topic Wikivoyage/USC citations seen in money-017 and lan-ref-003. For each claim sentence, best = the eligible source with the highest citationSupport(sentence, source) >= bar. NUMERIC GUARD: every number token in the sentence (/\d[\d,.]*/, normalized by stripping commas) must appear in that source's title+body, else the sentence gets no source. This blocks memory figures such as lan-rsn-004's '1.2 billion' and cooking-001's 'danger zone' temperatures. Attach [best+1] only if at least 50% of claim sentences (and at least 1) found a source. Otherwise return the text unchanged with added=[]. File: kiln-local/rs-H4/src/routing/answer.ts. Add module const READ_GROUND = typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env?.BOAR_READ_GROUND === '1'; and READ_GROUND_BAR = Number(process.env?.BOAR_READ_GROUND_BAR ?? 0.6). Hook: right after the existing attributeCitations block (about l.1584-1591) and BEFORE the verdictGuard block and the 'allCitationsRemoved ... release("all-citations-removed")' line (l.1604). Only when READ_GROUND && !health && gen.mode !== 'multipass' && sources.length && text.trim() && !/\[\d+\]/.test(text) && isCompactModel(genLlm) && !stopRequested: const g = groundUncited(text, sources.map((c) => fullOf(c)), req.query, READ_GROUND_BAR). If g.added.length: text = g.text; finalText = text; reasonCodes.push('citations:grounded-' + g.added.join('-')). The downstream checks then see [n]: the all-citations-removed and uncited-with-sources releases do not fire, and finish() computes cited. Do not change ATTRIBUTION_MIN_SUPPORT, CT-1 or any 4B path. Adapter metadata: add 'engine.read_ground' and 'engine.read_ground_bar' to the run-metadata spread in adapter.ts (about l.859). Checks: (a) tsc --noEmit is clean, plus unit tests for groundUncited covering the lan-cmp-004 shape (moose plus bison chunks gets [n]), the lan-rsn-004 shape (memory number, no [n]), an off-topic source (no [n]) and the 50% rule. (b) Byte-identity with the switch unset on the replay, which this hook does not affect. (c) 0-LLM offline pre-count before any generation: a small node script that imports groundUncited and applies it to the F1b answer texts in rnd/research/coordinator/arms/coverage-map/sefix/ans-traces (f1b-main-s42.traces.jsonl) with the keptFull sources from sefix/replays/main.v3-extra.jsonl, then lists the items that would flip from warned to cited. Expect money-003, vit-cry-001, lan-cmp-004 and lan-exp-002 among them. Inspect each flip by hand for memory content before the screen. Generation is still needed for the screen because the warning changes the released text.
fixes.expected_effect: The 'Not found ... from the model's memory' prefix is removed from correct answers that rest on kept text. The judge docked that prefix by about 0.5-1.0 (lan-exp-002: 3.5 warned vs 4.5 cited in ARM-G; money-003: 3.0 vs 2.0). Expected +0.5 correctness on 2-4 of the 5 targets, and ΔU +0.02 to +0.04 on the changed items. The changed set is small (the pre-count bounds it). This is the criterion's predicted cite-or-ground reader.
fixes.risk: CE-unwarned is the hard gate: a memory answer that shares 60% of its key terms with an on-topic chunk loses its warning. Mitigations are the query-overlap eligibility, the numeric guard, the 50%-of-sentences rule, and the offline pre-count with manual review of every flip. If the pre-count flips any item whose F1b judge correctness is below 2.5, raise the bar to 0.67 before generating, and log it in the arm notes, since the criterion freezes the rule and not this parameter. It does not lift correctness where the key fact is absent (vit-cry-001 likely stays at about 2). Distinct from DECODE-GROUND, which lost citations via the prompt: this is post-processing only.

fixes.name: READ-KEEPANS: compression floor and thread keep for SE answer chunks
fixes.env_switch: BOAR_READ_KEEPANS=1 (optional BOAR_READ_KEEPANS_TOKENS, default 250); unset = byte-identical F1b
fixes.spec: File: kiln-local/rs-H4/src/routing/answer.ts. Add module consts READ_KEEPANS = typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env?.BOAR_READ_KEEPANS === '1' and KEEPANS_TOKENS = Number(process.env?.BOAR_READ_KEEPANS_TOKENS ?? 250). Hook: immediately after 'const compressed = compressContext(matchQuery, raw, { tokenBudget: budget, pinned }); let sources = compressed.chunks;' (about l.1063-1064) and BEFORE the grounding/topic guard. Only when READ_KEEPANS && !health && gen?.mode !== 'multipass': sources = restoreSeAnswers(sources, raw, approxTokens, KEEPANS_TOKENS). Put restoreSeAnswers as an exported pure function in src/rag/compress.ts with unit tests. isSeAnswer is the same as in READ-SEQ (chunkId /^pack:local-qa-/ and body /^Answers >/); export it from one place if both arms land, otherwise duplicate it locally. Algorithm, with extra = 0 and cap = KEEPANS_TOKENS: (1) WHOLE: for each kept chunk k (in kept order) that isSeAnswer by its raw version r = raw.find(x => x.chunkId === k.chunkId), with r.body.length <= 1000 and k.body !== r.body: delta = approxTokens(r.body) - approxTokens(k.body). If extra + delta <= cap, replace k.body with r.body (the full chunk) and add delta to extra. Push 'keepans:whole:<chunkId>'. (2) THREAD: for each raw chunk r not in sources that isSeAnswer with r.body.length <= 1000, whose docId equals the docId of some chunk already in sources (its question or another answer), taking raw order: if extra + approxTokens(r.title + r.body) <= cap, insert r directly after the last sources chunk with the same docId and add its tokens to extra. Push 'keepans:thread:<chunkId>'. Restored chunks then pass through the existing grounding, topic guard and head pass unchanged (no exemption from the topic guard in this arm). Leave compressContext itself unchanged, so FAST_CONTEXT_TOKENS and the other callers are byte-identical. Adapter metadata: 'engine.read_keepans' and 'engine.read_keepans_tokens' in adapter.ts (about l.859). Checks: (a) tsc --noEmit is clean, plus unit tests (money-016-shaped: an 881-char chunk is not whole because it exceeds 1000? no, 881 <= 1000, so it is restored whole; the cap is respected; a non-SE chunk is untouched). (b) Byte-identity with the switch unset: replay-retrieval.sh on MAIN 97 vs sefix/replays/main.v3-extra.jsonl. (c) With the switch on, the replay must show money-016 keeping the '[usage detail removed]K' sentence and money-020 keeping chunk 136998 (if the topic guard still drops 136998, record it as a negative finding). Report the mean prompt-token increase over MAIN 97 (must stay <= +15% relative, else lower KEEPANS_TOKENS to 150 and re-replay before generating). Then list the changed ids for the divergence-first Haiku screen.
fixes.expected_effect: The fact sentence returns to the prompt in the 2 class-c items, plus the second fact sentence in money-018 and cooking-001. Prior: +0.5 to +1.0 on 1-3 targets, if the 1.7B then reads it (class a shows that presence alone is not enough). Expected ΔU +0.01 to +0.03 on the changed items. This is the weakest of the three and is most useful stacked with READ-SEQ.
fixes.risk: (1) A longer prompt means more prefill on the phone (up to +250 tokens, about +1.5 s on the iPhone 13 class) and more crowding, so a junk-heavy context gets longer. That is why the cap and the token check exist. (2) Restoring a whole answer chunk brings back throwaway sentences that can pull a 1.7B off the fact. (3) The thread restore can re-add an answer of the right thread that disagrees with the fact chunk (cooking-012 pattern). (4) Small target set (2 strict class-c items), so the 'target mean correctness +0.5' clause is noisy on n=4.

synthesis.summary:
The frozen criterion checks out (READER-criterion.md, sha f361f738…a38ac4). The autopsy has 62 rows covering 44 unique ids; 9 ids were classified twice with conflicting classes and I reconciled them on evidence.

Class counts (n=44): a ignored/memory 12, b used-uncited-warned 4, c compressed out 2, d SE answer without its question 0, e rubric mismatch 4, f other 22. The f group splits into: fact not actually kept 11 (delivery false positive), success/no-harm 9, SE question-body echo 2.

The prediction "a+b ≥ 60%" holds only on the 24 items where the fact is really in the kept context and the answer failed: (12+4)/24 = 67%. Over all 44 it is 36%. Three reader-side switches, each default-off with byte-identity checked by the retrieval replay against sefix/replays/main.v3-extra.jsonl:
